newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World sees rising oils/fats import demand.
newsitem.headline: Oil World sees rising oils/fats import demand.

text.p: Net global imports of oils and fats were forecast at 7.6 million tonnes in April/Sept 1997, up 14 percent from the same period last year and 12 percent from Oct/March 96/97, independent newsletter Oil World said.
Most additional imports would be made by China, followed by Turkey, Iraq, Mexico and Venezuela, it said.
Competitive prices meant soy oil and sun oil would be relatively more in demand up to May/June than palm and rape oil.

World production of oils and fats would see an usually sharp seasonal decline and stocks were low, said the report, based on 14 oils and fats excluding sesame, olive and castor oil, in 20 major countries.
Global stocks of 14 oils and fats on April 1 were estimated at 3.1 million tonnes, down from 3.8 million a year ago, when they had exceeded the 1995 figure by one million.
Chinese stocks were sharply down but Hong Kong was raising its stocks ahead of reunification and because of higher vegetable oils prices in mainland China, Oil World noted.

Domestic consumption of the 14 products in the 20 countries was forecast to rise to 19.9 million tonnes in April/September, five percent up on the same 1996 period. -Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
